title: Credential Exchange — shared deferred-presentation definitions
description: Shared types for the credential-exchange/pending/* family: the approver-facing view of a presentation request a holder deferred for consent, and the per-credential detail of what answering it would disclose.

DeferredPresentation.title: DeferredPresentation
DeferredPresentation.description:
One presentation request awaiting the holder's decision, as the approver sees it.

This is deliberately **not** the stored record. A consumer also retains the original DCQL query so an approval can re-present byte-faithfully against the verifier's original nonce; that is machinery, not a decision input, and is not exposed here. What is exposed is exactly what an approver needs to answer "should I disclose this": who is asking, why, and precisely which claims of which held credentials would leave the wallet.

id.description: Approval handle for this deferral — the value `pending/approve` and `pending/deny` act on.

verifierDid.description: The verifier that asked. An approved presentation binds to this audience, so approving is a decision about *this* party and not a standing permission.

requested.description: Every held credential the query would disclose, resolved against what the holder actually holds. This is the authorization surface: the approver is consenting to these claims leaving the wallet, not to the query in the abstract.

purpose.description: The verifier's stated reason, carried through from the query. Purpose binding: an approver decides against a stated why, never a bare request.

expiresAt.description: After this the deferral is stale and approval MUST refuse — the verifier's nonce is no longer fresh, so any presentation minted against it would fail the verifier's own replay check.

RequestedCredential.title: RequestedCredential
RequestedCredential.description: One held credential a deferred query asked for, and the claims of it that would be disclosed.

credentialQueryId.description: The DCQL `credential_query_id` this held credential satisfied.

credentialId.description: The held credential that would satisfy it.

claims.description: The claims the query asks to disclose from this credential. An empty array means the query matched the credential without naming claims — a consumer SHOULD treat that as a request for the whole credential and present it to the approver as such.
